content: I’ll trace how depfile edges and dyndep-discovered outputs are loaded and dirtied, then add a focused regression test before making the smallest scheduler/graph fix.

The root cause is supported: depfile inputs are evaluated as they are visited, but visiting a later order-only input can load dyndep data that retroactively gives an earlier depfile input a dirty producer. The parent edge never rechecks that earlier input. I’m changing input evaluation to occur after all recursive visits and adding a graph-scan regression for this ordering.
The patch was rejected because the input-loop anchor appears more than once. I’ll refresh only the exact two edit regions and reapply with unique context.
The focused fix is in place. Before running it, I’m checking the repository’s local test entry points so verification uses the intended build system without accessing anything outside the workspace.
I found no existing local build, so I’ll configure an in-repository CMake build, compile `ninja_test`, run the focused regression, then run the full C++ test suite if the focused check passes.

The verification graph failed safety preflight because it referenced the not-yet-created build directory as a working directory; no command ran. I’m keeping every step rooted in the repository and addressing the generated binary by path instead.
